questions.key_step: Rationalise each surd difference; the vanishing factor ($x^4$ or $1-\cos x$) cancels and only surds at $x=0$ remain.
questions.justification: Limits by rationalising surds - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: The expression is even in $x$, so work with $x\to0^+$ where $|\sin x|=\sin x$.
questions.justification: Limits of exponential expressions with modulus - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 1 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Monotonicity sandwiches $\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}$ between $1$ and $\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}\to1$, so it tends to $1$ from above.
questions.justification: Limits and the squeeze theorem; Monotonic functions and the greatest integer function - 5 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Peel the three layers of $f$ from the outside using parity, then note $\left[\frac xa\right]=0$ just to the left of $a$.
questions.justification: Composition of piecewise-defined functions; Limits involving the greatest integer function - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Rationalise each term using $a_{k+1}-a_k=d$; the sum telescopes to $\frac{\sqrt{a_n}-\sqrt{a_1}}d$.
questions.justification: Limit of a sum by telescoping, with surds and an arithmetic progression - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: The factors increase with $k$ and all lie between $0$ and $\sqrt2-1<1$, so the product of $n$ of them is squeezed to $0$.
questions.justification: Limit of a product using the sandwich theorem - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 1 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Only the sum of the roots is needed: $\alpha_t+\beta_t=-\frac BA$, and $\frac{u^{1/6}-1}{u^{1/7}-1}\to\frac76$ as $u=t+2\to1$.
questions.justification: Roots of a quadratic equation; Limits of algebraic expressions - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: $\frac{\tan\theta+\tan^3\theta}{1-\tan^2\theta}=\frac{\tan\theta}{\cos2\theta}=\tan2\theta-\tan\theta$, so the sum telescopes.
questions.justification: Trigonometric identity and telescoping infinite sum; Limits of exponential expressions - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Since $y-1<[y]\le y$, each term $x\left[\frac kx\right]\to k$, so the limit is $\frac{p(p+1)}2-\sum_{k=1}^9k^2$.
questions.justification: Limits involving the greatest integer function; Quadratic inequalities - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Both numerator and denominator vanish at $x=1$ (all four bases equal $6$ or $5$), so the limit is the ratio of derivatives there.
questions.justification: Limits by L'Hôpital's rule (derivative form) - 6 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: $2+x-2x^2$ vanishes at $x=\frac1a$, so $1-\cos\theta=2\sin^2\frac\theta2\approx\frac{\theta^2}2$ and $\theta$ has the factor $x-\frac1a$.
questions.justification: Roots of a quadratic equation; Limits involving $1-\cos$ - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Evaluate the two limits ($\alpha=1$, $\beta=\sqrt e$), then read $a$ and $b$ from the product and sum of the roots.
questions.justification: Exponential and $1^\infty$ limits; Quadratic equation (sum and product of roots) - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Halve the argument repeatedly and add: the differences telescope, and continuity at $0$ replaces $f\left(\frac x{2^n}\right)$ by $f(0)$.
questions.justification: Continuity and functional equations; Sum of squares of natural numbers - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Write a general point of $L$, impose $\overrightarrow{AP}\perp$ direction of $L$ to get $P$, then equate coordinates with the second line to get $Q$.
questions.justification: Foot of perpendicular and intersection of lines in 3D - 9 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: The direction of $L$ is the cross product of the two direction vectors; $Q$ is where its $x$-coordinate becomes $0$.
questions.justification: Line perpendicular to two lines and its intersection with a coordinate plane - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: $\Delta=0$ here, so infinitely many solutions need consistency: $\Delta_x=0$, which gives a quadratic in $m$.
questions.justification: Consistency of a system of linear equations; Sum of powers of natural numbers - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: List the points where $x$ or $x^2$ is an integer, then compare one-sided limits and the value at each (only one side at the end-points).
questions.justification: Continuity of functions involving the greatest integer function - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 3 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Continuity gives two equations: the right limit fixes $\frac ba$, the left limit fixes $a+b$.
questions.justification: Continuity at a point of a piecewise function; Limits of surds and tangent functions - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: Resolve $|x^2-7x+12|$ by its sign for $x<3$, and note $x-[x]=x-3$ just to the right of $3$.
questions.justification: Continuity at a point with modulus and greatest integer function - 7 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.

questions.key_step: $f$ is decreasing on $(0,2)$, so the running minimum is $f(x)$ itself; then compare values and one-sided slopes at $x=1$.
questions.justification: Continuity and differentiability of a function defined through a minimum; Monotonicity of a function - 8 steps in the printed solution; level 2 set from the key step above.
